title: (new, the owner's order 11-18 18:18): surround output by a written law. The two-channel output stays as made.
note: File 08 5.H.5. The law (pan and surround amounts to speaker gains for each layout the device reports: Windows' channel mask, Android's report) written in the inventory before the code, after reading the game's sound code and the mixer. Properties asserted by tests over the whole range for every layout: the power equals two channels' at every value, no gain jump, left and right mirrored, no inverted or matrix-encoded signal on a speaker of its own, the device's channel order, a defined fold for fewer speakers. A render-to-file test through the real mixer per layout. Windows and Android; Linux and Mac build. 11-18 (the harness's Sound report, checked at 241395b49): the game's send gains already apply a matrix rear curve, sin((x * 0.34776 + 0.32612) * pi / 2) for every send whose second curve is 3 or 7, in every output mode, before the device's layout is known (SoundVoices.cpp:772 in mixerVolumes, :704-786); the law takes the rear amount before that curve, in the game's sends, with the buses named (P-221). The bus set includes the matrix encoding's inverted right (SoundEngine.cpp:16-21): kept for two channels, never on a speaker of its own. 11-18 (the harness's platform/sdl report, checked at 241395b49): the SDL hosts open their stream with two channels always (audio_device_sdl.cpp:33); the device's format is read only for its rate (:17-20), so P-193's discrete path cannot be reached on Android or Linux until the stream takes the device's channel count and order. 11-18 (the harness's runtime/src report, checked at 241395b49): the places the law reaches: the speaker list knows seven positions, LFE among the silent Others (audio_device.h:12); WASAPI opens the device's mask only when surround is asked and the mask has side or back bits (audio_device_wasapi.cpp:207-227), the stream with popcount(mask) channels (:179) against an 18-entry speaker list (:400); the discrete form hands out centre and one surround pair (audio_mixer.h:90-95), the surround buses still through the fold delays and the inverted bus subtracted from the right (audio_mixer.cpp:244-261); the panner's rear effect sends matrixed into effect lines 2 and 3 in both modes (:804-818); place() splits a rear bus equally over side and back speakers, sends the centre at -3 dB to left and right when there is no centre speaker, and clamps (native_audio.cpp:95-118); the two-channel path writes two values a frame for any device of two channels or fewer (:153, :158). 11-22 (the owner: 3.1, 5.1 and 7.1 in the game's options): the player chooses the speakers with one setting, Speakers (Auto, Mono, Stereo, Encoded stereo, 3.1, 5.1, 7.1), in place of Sound output; a layout with more speakers than the device reports is not offered; its texts in all 14 languages. The step is G6.7 (order 29 of the native plan, after the tablet's pacing steps); its card and the inventory's section 4 (points 10 and 11) hold the rest.

note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Sound report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. title: (console-era remnant, audio sync): the step learns that a music stream ended from the audio device. The audio thread counts a stream's finishes as the device takes its samples (StreamPlayer.hpp:26-28); StreamSound::finished compares that count on the game thread (StreamSound.cpp:122-124), tryDie_ kills the sound on it (:263-266), the handle detaches, and AudBgm::isStopping answers true (AudBgm.hpp:76-82), which MR::isPlayingStageBgm and its family read (SoundUtil.cpp:378-440; git grep -c -E 'MR::is(Playing|Stage)[A-Za-z]*(Bgm|BGM)' in native/petari/src: 32 lines). So the step on which a non-looping music ends follows the device's buffer and latency, and the ticks dropped after a stall (SoundEngine.cpp:151-160): the console's sound and picture ran from one clock.
note: Found by the readall harness's sound-area reports (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. The play position itself (the beat) is read only by the audio thread's sequence clock (TempoAdjuster::sequenceSeconds, RhythmSystem.cpp:100-110, set at :187): no step reads it. Modern form: a stream's end known by the step clock (its length in samples from the step it started, the audio following); the device never decides a step. Replay: the same on every device afterwards, not the same as each device's run today (a question for the owner only if today's runs must be matched).

title: (memory, sound handles): a handle taken over by a new sound stays pointed to by the old one. AudMeMgr::startMe stops the handle's old phrase only when its stop is timed and never detaches it (AudMePlayer.cpp:235-244); SpkSoundHolder's start stops or kills the old speaker sound without releasing the handle (SpkSound.cpp:151-166). attachHandle then points the handle at the new sound (AudMePlayer.cpp:76-82, SpkSound.cpp:74-81), and the old sound's releaseHandle, at its end, clears the handle and so drops the new sound (AudMePlayer.cpp:84-91, :186-194; SpkSound.cpp:34-35, :83-90); a handle freed first is written after its free. Also: a Me phrase's id indexes the parameter table unbounded (AudMePlayer.hpp:133-135), and a speaker sound's wave id is checked only for < 0 (SpkSound.cpp:147) before it indexes the speaker table and waves (:103-107).
note: Found by the readall harness's sound-area reports (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fix: a handle and its sound detach as a pair (the takeover releases the old owner); ids checked against their tables at start, an unknown one refused.

Replay identical.
